recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is recommended for FHIR-7887 unless PHER reopens the broader question of whether every Immunization must carry at least a narrative/string occurrence value.
issue_request: FHIR-7887 was a Published/Persuasive PHER core issue asking to make Immunization.date optional (0..1) because patient-reported immunizations may not have a specific known date, including cases where an adult cannot recall the year of a childhood immunization.
initial_application: The issue was explicitly applied in git commit b4d544060ae9468bc9fe06353a0af056866f9d28, which changed Immunization.date from 1..1 to 0..1 and added the Jira rationale as committee-comment text. Later source refactoring moved the element to Immunization.occurrence[x].
additional_context: Current Immunization is in build scope through the active source/fhir.ini resources entry. The current StructureDefinition carries committee note #7887 on Immunization.occurrence[x], keeps the patient-reported-date rationale in the comment, and permits dateTime or string. Later related issues support this design: FHIR-16223 considered unknown IPS immunization dates resolved by adopting R4, FHIR-18293 declined an interval for imprecise dates and documented string use when exact dates are unknown, and FHIR-46477 updated the same occurrence comment while preserving that rule.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. Changing occurrence[x] back to 0..1 would conflict with later applied/published design rather than complete the 2015 issue.

related_jiras.note: IPS unknown immunization date concern was recorded as resolved by adoption of R4, supporting the current dateTime|string approach.
PHER declined adding Period for imprecise immunization dates and documented string use when exact dates are unknown.
R6 Applied issue updated Immunization.occurrence[x] comments and preserved the FHIR-7887 patient-reported-date guidance.
Search parameter work confirms occurrence[x] can be string, while clinical-date search intentionally covers only dateTime values.
